newsitem.title: UK: London insurance bodies talk could lead to merger.
newsitem.headline: London insurance bodies talk could lead to merger.

text.p: The two main bodies representing insurance companies in the London market are in talks over creating a closer relationship which could eventually lead to a merger, market officials said on Wednesday.

The talks involved the Institute of London Underwriters (ILU), a market for marine insurance companies, and the London International Insurance and Reinsurance Association (LIRMA), a trade federation for non-marine insurance companies.
"What we are doing is exploring how we can co-operate better to create a more focused voice for the market," said ILU chief executive Tony Funnel.
He said there was no fixed agenda, but confirmed there was a possibility that merger could be discussed.

An industry source told Reuters that there is considerable support for a merger in terms of cutting costs and creating a single market voice for marketing and lobbying. For example, both organisations pay separate teams of lawyers in the U.S to do similar jobs. Such a move would also respond to government criticism that the insurance industry has too many bodies representing different sectors. LIRMA chief executive Marie-Louise Rossi said the bodies were discussing areas of further co-operation but said no formal merger talks were planned at present.
The ILU has a high profile around the world and works closely with Lloyd's of London on which it cooperates with many policies and wordings and shares ownership of The Salvage Association.

It owns its market building in Leadenhall Street in the City of London and like Lloyd's it has a network of arrangements around the world. But the closure of dozens of insurance companies after the heavy losses of the late 1980s, combined with the more recent spate of mergers, has caused the membership to dwindle from 114 companies a few years ago to 53 today.

LIRMA works more like a trade association and is less involved with the day to day business of insurance, however it shares several initiatives with the ILU, and together they own the London Processing Centre which handles electronic trading for each market. LIRMA is a tenant in the recently-opened London Underwriting Centre, but Funnell said that moving out of the ILU building was not up for negotiation. -- Reuters Insurance News +44 171 542 2770
